atlases.binding: pool_skimmer_activity.gd creates one AtlasTexture per index. Current first-two x origins are12 and352 with341-square windows and filter_clip; other four nominal regions remain unchanged. Six cells are live at62–88px fitted bounds. Cell scores below describe the earlier nominal-region source review; the implementation section records the bounded correction.

cells.observed_subject: torn pink star wrapper with white torn ends and green grime
cells.finding: Strong immediate litter identity and broad silhouette, but the wrapper reaches the x=341 cell cut and contributes strong-alpha pixels on its right boundary. Direct extraction clips the wrapper and can contaminate cell 1; dense torn-end detail may also soften at the 68px live size.

cells.observed_subject: crushed open silver can with green grime
cells.finding: Convincing hollow topology and material, but its left extraction boundary contains strong-alpha pixels inherited from the adjacent wrapper bleed. The gray interior can also lose separation over dark pool water.

cells.observed_subject: blue bottle cap or ring with green grime
cells.finding: Clean circular topology and bright cyan edge. Its pristine jewel-like finish competes with the intended trash read until grime is noticed.

cells.observed_subject: orange leaf with bubbles and green grime
cells.finding: Broad, phone-readable silhouette and clear vein structure. It is natural debris rather than manufactured litter, but remains semantically valid pool cleanup.

cells.observed_subject: twisted lavender ribbon or plastic strip with green grime
cells.finding: Thin folded topology is coherent at source scale but has the weakest contact footprint and most ambiguous identity at the 88px live bound.

cells.observed_subject: yellow porous sponge with bubbles and green grime
cells.finding: Strong silhouette and material readability. It may read as a usable cleaning tool rather than trash unless the mounted basket/dirty-water context disambiguates it.

atlases.consistency: All cells share saturated painted highlights, navy-purple contour treatment, bubble accents and green grime. Lighting and outline weight are internally consistent.

alpha_boundary_measurement.method: Read-only PIL alpha scan of each 341x341 extraction boundary on the exact e554c4f253bcaa9e5893d9e4fffe03feef96528211f2458dc5d8fc81299f56df sheet
alpha_boundary_measurement.interpretation: Cell 0 wrapper pixels reach the x=341 cut and bleed into cell 1. Cell 3 has no comparable strong-alpha boundary defect. Transparent gaps prove the sheet background is transparent; the black/dark presentation in image viewing is not a painted rectangle.

atlases.contact_topology: The subjects have no authored waterline or contact shadow, so water ownership depends on the runtime ripple and skimmer overlap. Cells 2-5 preserve isolated topology at their inspected boundaries. Cells 0 and 1 do not: the wrapper crosses their shared atlas cut, clipping cell 0 and contaminating cell 1. Cell 4's narrow ribbon and cell 1's dark cavity need additional mounted contact scrutiny.

visual_dimensions.finding: The family is polished and internally coherent, but the measured cell-0/cell-1 boundary bleed is a concrete extraction defect. Cells 2, 4 and 5 also weaken immediate trash identity and cell 4 weakens small-scale readability.

source_dimension_check.finding: The 1023x682 file exactly fits a 3x2 grid of 341px cells and stays within the <=1024 texture rule. Each source cell has ample pixels for its 62-88px runtime size. NPOT dimensions are legal at this size but should not use a POT-only compression assumption.

motion.reason: One static subject per cell. The sheet cannot establish idle drift, skimmer intersection, flight cadence or basket arrival.

cell 1 left boundary contains neighboring wrapper pixels
